1930, February
FATHER SOLANUS, NOTEBOOK NO. 1.
Page 41 Cont.
Febr Joseph Modell - Nerveous & impatient now - improved decidedly in indegestion
Febr. 11 Mrs. Clark about 40 reports this morning - her arm in a sling, that having slipped on the ice last Wednesday and broken her arm. She said nothing about it at home till next day when it was quite swolen and doctor pronounced it "seemingly broken," but decided not to touch it till Xrayed. "In the mean time I promised to Poor Souls a perpetual enrolment if no
Page 42
Febr 22 (Wash. Birthday) James H. Smick sentenced to death - to be elec- tricuted Nov. 29 last, was enrolled Nov 3rd Execution of sentence was postponed till Jan. 30th following. when again postponed to 28th this month.
March 4th Robert Hopp. 52 of 3626 Palmer (Father non Catholic) given up last Wednesday (Feb 26) Tubercular Spinal manegitis, enrolled March 1st (Pd $3) Is sleeping well since enrolled. To-day mother insists on paying another dollar - the last she has - Husband has promised to be instructed.
5th Mrs. Freeda Genrinck 34, (544 Jefferson Court) mother of two, can- cerous breast removed last Nov: Other now starting and otherwise coming back all over scar and on neck. Enrolled about a month ago no improvement as yet. In fact end is expected shortly.
April 2nd Francis Leeson 11 4684 - 18th St heart & nerveous in bed near half the day Enrolled To-day 1 year Mother anxious and promising perpetual if improved.
April 3rd Mastoid Phyllis Blake 7 (of 1138 Nottingham Rd G. Point Pk. ), took measles about a month ago. Two weeks later her ears started to run. Last Saturday March 29 was screaming from pain when moth- er phoned to have her enrolled. Improvement followed, but Dr. pronounced double mastoid. She was taken to St. Mary's Hospital 30th March Yesterday, two doctors and two nurses came in to oper ate - little head shaved & all ready. Mother pleads: "Don't cut her." I. And To-day Phyllis is brought to Monastery, smiling, on her way home from Hospital. II. Mother and grandmother came last night and had her name once more inscribed in Mass Assoc'n
